questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Agree TO Proposal vs Agree WITH Person
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition:
"The Full Court Bench unanimously agreed ___ the registrar's recommendation regarding digital courtroom recording."
questions.explanation: Target yahan 'recommendation' (formal proposal/advice) hai. Formal recommendation ya proposal ko accept karne ke liye strictly 'agree TO' lagta hai: 'agreed to the recommendation'. Agar target registrar vyakti hota, tab 'agreed with the registrar' hota.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: Confusing Relational Pairs — Agree TO a proposal/recommendation.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12 Certification

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Direct Transitive Verbs: Zero Preposition with 'Discuss'
questions.question: Select the sentence that is grammatically free from error:

options.text: The committee discussed about the new IT policy before submitting the final draft.
The committee discussed the new IT policy before submitting the final draft.
The committee discussed on the new IT policy before submitting the final draft.
The committee discussed for the new IT policy before submitting the final draft.

questions.explanation: 'Discuss' direct transitive verb hai jiske baad bina kisi preposition ke seedhe direct object 'the new IT policy' aata hai. 'About' ya 'on' lagana redundant pleonasm hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: The Direct Transitive Law — Discuss (NO about!).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12 Certification

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition:
"The new optical fiber network is vastly superior ___ the legacy copper cabling in data transmission speed."
questions.explanation: Latin origin ke comparative adjectives (superior, inferior, senior, junior, prior) comparison mein hamesha preposition 'TO' lete hain, 'than' nahi.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: Comparative Preposition Law — Words ending in -or take 'TO'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12 Certification

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition:
"The accused was prosecuted because he was accused ___ leaking sensitive judicial records."
questions.explanation: Apradh ya violation ka dosh lagane ke liye 'accused OF' formula hota hai ('accused of leaking'). 'Accused for' bolna fatal examination error hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Causal & Result Vectors — Accuse OF a crime.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12 Certification

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence:

options.text: The entire administrative staff looks forward to attend the Chief Justice's farewell.
The entire administrative staff looks forward to attending the Chief Justice's farewell.
The entire administrative staff looks forward for attending the Chief Justice's farewell.
The entire administrative staff looks forward at attending the Chief Justice's farewell.

questions.explanation: 'Look forward to' mein 'to' preposition hai, isliye iske baad verb hamesha GERUND (-ing form) mein aayegi: 'look forward to attending'. Bare infinitive 'attend' lagana wrong hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Preposition + Gerund Law — look forward to + V-ING.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12 Certification

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Direct Transitive Verbs: Physical Space Entry
questions.question:
Spot the error in the sentence:
"The senior advocate / entered into the courtroom / just as the case was called out. / No error"

options.text: just as the case was called out.

questions.explanation: Physical enclosed space (courtroom, chamber, hall) mein pravesh ke liye 'enter' direct object leta hai: 'entered the courtroom'. Yahan 'into' lagana redundant preposition error hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: The Direct Transitive Law — Physical room entry takes zero preposition.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12 Certification

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition:
"For quick disposal of commercial disputes, business houses prefer mediation ___ prolonged adversarial litigation."
questions.explanation: Verb 'prefer' do entities ke beech preference comparison mein hamesha preposition 'TO' demand karta hai: 'prefer mediation TO litigation'.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: Comparative Preposition Law — Prefer X TO Y (Never Than!).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12 Certification

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Causal Vectors: Result IN vs Result FROM
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition:
"Unsecured network configurations frequently result ___ unauthorized intrusion into judicial databases."
questions.explanation: Subject 'Unsecured network configurations' Kaaran (Cause) hai aur object 'unauthorized intrusion' Parinaam (Outcome) hai. Cause se outcome ki taraf forward vector hamesha 'RESULT IN' leta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Causal & Result Vectors — Cause resulted IN Outcome.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12 Certification

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition:
"The computer typist is exceptionally good ___ maintaining flawless speed in high-pressure hearings."
questions.explanation: Kisi skill, speed ya craft mein nipun hone ke liye standard English collocation strictly 'GOOD AT' hai ('good at maintaining').
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: Evaluative & Emotional Adjectives — Good AT for skill/competence.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12 Certification

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Spot the error in the sentence:
"The Chief Justice Bench / disposed off fifty / pending PILs in a marathon session. / No error"

options.text: pending PILs in a marathon session.

questions.explanation: Legal disposal of petitions, cases ya files ke liye collocation hamesha single 'f' wala 'DISPOSE OF' hoti hai. 'Disposed off' (double 'f') misspelling aur grammatical error hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Statutory & Administrative Preposition Concord — Dispose OF (Single 'f' always!).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12 Certification

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition:
"The division bench observed that alternate dispute resolution is an effective solution ___ trial court congestion."
questions.explanation: Noun 'solution' kisi samasya ya congestion ke liye preposition 'TO' demand karta hai: 'solution TO congestion'. 'Solution of' non-standard hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: Noun + Preposition Syntactic Units — Solution TO a problem.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12 Certification

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correct verb form:
"The state government amended the service regulations with a view to ___ higher efficiency in judicial administration."
questions.explanation: 'With a view to' ke baad aane wali verb mandatory GERUND (-ing form) hoti hai: 'with a view to achieving'.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Preposition + Gerund Law — With a view to + V-ING.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12 Certification

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition:
"The IT vendor failed to comply ___ the data security protocols mandated in the service tender."
questions.explanation: Standard administrative English mein 'comply' hamesha preposition 'WITH' leta hai ('comply with protocols/rules').
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Statutory & Administrative Preposition Concord — Comply WITH regulations.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12 Certification

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition:
"The appellate bench acquitted the judicial assistant ___ the charge of gross dereliction of duty."
questions.explanation: 'Acquit' kisi person ko arop ya apradh se bari karne ke liye strictly preposition 'OF' leta hai: 'acquitted the assistant OF the charge'.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Statutory & Administrative Preposition Concord — Acquit OF the charge.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12 Certification

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question: Which of the following sentences is 100% grammatically correct in standard English?

options.text: The advocate discussed about the case and claimed to be senior than all prosecutors.
He entered into the courtroom and ordered for the certified copy of the decree.
He was accused of embezzlement, but the bench agreed to his plea for an adjournment.
The committee looked forward to inspect the court files and disposed off twenty petitions.

questions.explanation: Option C 100% correct hai: 'accused OF embezzlement' (correct collocation) aur 'agreed TO his plea' (formal plea/request ke liye 'agree to' standard hai). Option A mein 'discussed about' aur 'senior than' galat hain; Option B mein 'entered into the courtroom' aur 'ordered for' galat hain; Option D mein 'looked forward to inspect' (should be inspecting) aur 'disposed off' (should be of) galat hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rules RC-04, RC-05, RC-08, RC-10: Comprehensive Fixed Preposition Architecture.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12 Certification
